prompt:
Research what Let's Encrypt officially states about its certificate rate limits (certificates per registered domain, duplicate certificates, failed validations). Cite the official page.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Let’s Encrypt officially describes a main weekly cap per registered domain, a separate duplicate/renewal cap, and an hourly failed-validation cap; the same official documentation also notes that revoking certificates does not reset these limits, and the staging environment is recommended for debugging because limits are higher there.

SOURCE: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/ | QUOTE: "The main limit is Certificates per Registered Domain (50 per week)." | CLAIM: The primary certificate issuance limit is 50 certificates per registered domain per week.
SOURCE: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/ | QUOTE: "A registered domain is, generally speaking, the part of the domain you purchased from your domain name registrar." | CLAIM: “Registered domain” means the registrable domain (e.g., example.com), based on the public suffix plus one label.
SOURCE: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/ | QUOTE: "Renewals are treated specially: they don't count against your Certificates per Registered Domain limit, but they are subject to a Duplicate Certificate limit of 5 per week." | CLAIM: Renewals don’t count against the 50/week registered-domain limit, but duplicates are limited to 5 per week.
SOURCE: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/ | QUOTE: "A certificate is considered a renewal (or a duplicate) of an earlier certificate if it contains the exact same set of hostnames, ignoring capitalization and ordering of hostnames." | CLAIM: “Duplicate certificate” is determined by the exact same hostname set (case/order-insensitive).
SOURCE: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/ | QUOTE: "There is a Failed Validation limit of 5 failures per account, per hostname, per hour." | CLAIM: Failed validations are limited to 5 per account per hostname per hour.
SOURCE: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/ | QUOTE: "This limit is higher on our staging environment, so you can use that environment to debug connectivity problems." | CLAIM: The staging environment has higher failed-validation limits and is intended for troubleshooting.
SOURCE: https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/ | QUOTE: "Revoking certificates does not reset rate limits, because the resources used to issue those certificates have already been consumed." | CLAIM: Revocation does not reset or refund rate-limit capacity.
